safety.en: The park was enjoyable, but the surrounding traffic, crossings and busy central streets needed attention.

scenery.en: Views across the city from the hills, with a very different sea view on the waterfront runs.

surface.en: Park paths in the hills and a flatter paved promenade beside the sea offer different running options.

access.en: I would choose the seafront for a beginner or an easier outing. The hills take more effort and navigation.

experience.en: Several return visits and two very different ways to enjoy a run, even when ten kilometres became sixteen.

en.title: Barcelona: hills, sea views and an accidental 16 km
en.excerpt: A planned 10 km run became 16.02 km in the hills around Park Güell. For an easier outing, I headed down to the flat seafront.
en.body:
I have been running in **Barcelona several times now**, and most of those runs have taken me up into the hills around **Park Güell**. There are climbs, city views and plenty of other people out for a jog. Down by the sea, Barcelona offers a very different run: flatter, easier to settle into and, for most people, probably the better place to begin.

On the hilly outing in this story, I planned to run **10 km**. I got lost, and the activity ended up at **16.02 km**. A slightly longer tour of the neighbourhood than intended. :)

## How I discovered the upper part of Barcelona

I was staying with my friend **Marc**, who had just finished setting up his co-living and co-working space. Staying in that part of the city is what led me to explore the hills near Park Güell with my running shoes on.

The park I ran around was a lovely little place, with lots of other joggers. Getting up to the top came with a good view over Barcelona. I have returned to this side of the city for runs on more than one visit.

![A broad path between trees and stone walls near Casa Trias in Park Güell](/assets/uploads/barcelona-hills-and-seafront/park-guell-path.jpg "A path near Casa Trias in Park Güell.")

Photo: [Joe Mabel / Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Park_G%C3%BCell_-_just_below_Casa_Trias_01.jpg), [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Resized.

I am describing the park area and the surrounding hills here. For current visitor access to Park Güell itself, check the [official park information](https://parkguell.barcelona/en/planning-your-visit/faqs).

## Ten kilometres, give or take another six

The supplied activity records **16.02 km**, with an average pace of approximately **5:42/km**, calculated from the activity's recorded time. The plan had been much simpler: go out for ten kilometres and come back. A few wrong turns took care of the rest.

There was plenty of uphill running. Once outside the park, there was also **a lot of traffic**, so I needed to be much more careful. The park paths and the surrounding streets felt like two different parts of the outing.

![Elevation profile of the Barcelona run, showing several climbs](/assets/uploads/barcelona-hills-and-seafront/elevation-profile.svg "The elevation profile from my activity. Distances along the GPX line are approximate.")

## The easier option: down by the sea

On other outings, I went down to the seafront for easier jogs. These were separate runs from the hilly activity above. **The waterfront is much flatter**, with the sea beside you and less climbing to think about.

For a beginner, or for a day when I just wanted a straightforward run, this would be my choice. I enjoyed the hills, but the seafront seemed a better fit for most people who simply want to put on their shoes and go for a jog in Barcelona.

![The broad paved Barceloneta promenade running beside the beach and sea](/assets/uploads/barcelona-hills-and-seafront/barceloneta-promenade.jpg "The promenade beside Barceloneta beach.")

Photo: [DimiTalen / Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Promenade_and_beach,_Platja_de_la_Barceloneta,_Barcelona,_2015.jpg), [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Resized.

## The streets between the good bits

Running through central Barcelona was more awkward. Between pedestrian crossings, tourists and traffic, I kept having to watch where I was going. At times it felt like slaloming between people rather than settling into a run.

That is the distinction I would keep in mind when choosing where to run here: **the hills for climbing and city views, or the seafront for a flatter outing**. Getting between them through busy streets needs a bit more patience and attention.

## A note about the photos

I lost my own Barcelona photos when I changed phones, so the photographs in this story are licensed images from other photographers. They illustrate the places, rather than documenting my runs.

**If you are local and have a couple of photos of the running paths or seafront that you would be happy for me to use, I would love to add them.** You can reach me on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/markuskaljuste/).
